import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A normal distribution is defined by mean and variance.",
            "The mean represents the center of the distribution.",
            "The variance defines the spread or noise level.",
            "Visually, we represent this as a bell curve.",
            "It shows certainty centered around the mean."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Shape of Certainty", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Gaussian function
        def gaussian(x, mu, sigma):
            return (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mu) / sigma)**2)

        # Create base Gaussian curve
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.5)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: gaussian(x, 0, 1), color=WHITE)
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[-1, 1], color="#ADD8E6", opacity=0.3)
        
        # Add Asset: bell icon
        bell_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg").scale(0.5).set_color(WHITE)
        
        plot_group = VGroup(axes, curve, area, bell_icon)
        
        # Positioning as requested by VideoCritic (Issue 23)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group, 'B3', 'E6', scale_factor=0.65)
        
        # Positioning the bell icon on top or side of the curve
        bell_icon.next_to(axes, UP)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(bell_icon), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#90EE90"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F08080"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(area), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FFD700"), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Rule: Summation of Parameters", [
            "The sum of two independent gaussians is gaussian.",
            "The new mean is the sum of means.",
            "The new variance is the sum of variances.",
            "Note that variances add, not standard deviations.",
            "This creates a predictable model for total time."
        ])
        
        # Prep objects
        g1_text = MathTex(r"N(\mu_1, \sigma_1^2)", color=WHITE)
        g2_text = MathTex(r"N(\mu_2, \sigma_2^2)", color=WHITE)
        sum_formula = MathTex(
            r"\mu_{sum} = \mu_1 + \mu_2 \\",
            r"\sigma_{sum}^2 = \sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2", 
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        clock = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/clock.svg")
        hourglass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hourglass.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(g1_text, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(g2_text, 'B6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(clock, 'A4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(g1_text), Write(g2_text), FadeIn(clock))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_in_area(sum_formula, 'C3', 'D6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_formula[0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Write(sum_formula[1]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        warning = Text("!", font_size=40, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(warning, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(warning))
        self.play(FadeOut(warning))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.place_at_grid(hourglass, 'F4', scale_factor=0.5)
        final_box = SurroundingRectangle(sum_formula, color=GOLD)
        self.play(Create(final_box), FadeIn(hourglass))
        self.wait(2)

        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Table showing summation rule: N1 + N2 = N_sum
        table = VGroup(
            Text("N(μ1, σ1²)", font_size=24, color=BLUE),

            Text("N(μ2, σ2²)", font_size=24, color=BLUE),

        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.4)

        curve2 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-(x-0.5)**2/0.5), color=BLUE)

        plot_group = VGroup(axes, curve1, curve2, combined_curve)

outline.topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Shape of Certainty
sections.content: Briefly define a Normal Distribution (Gaussian) by its two parameters: mean (μ) representing the center, and variance (σ²) representing the 'spread' or 'noise'. Introduce the visual representation as a symmetrical 'Bell Curve'.
sections.example: Imagine a robot cat fetching snacks; the time it takes follows a Bell Curve centered at 5 minutes.

sections.title: The Problem: Adding Two Independent Random Variables
sections.content: Pose the question: If we have two independent sources of random noise, what happens when we combine them? Visually represent two distinct Bell Curves moving toward each other and merging into one.
sections.example: A cat walks to the kitchen (X ~ N(μ1, σ1²)) and then spends time hunting for a toy (Y ~ N(μ2, σ2²)). How do we describe the total time (X + Y)?

sections.title: The Rule: Summation of Parameters
sections.content: Explain the elegant result: The sum remains Gaussian. The new mean is the sum of the means (μ_new = μ1 + μ2), and the new variance is the sum of the variances (σ²_new = σ1² + σ2²). Emphasize that variances add, not standard deviations.
sections.example: If the cat's travel time is N(5, 1) and hunting time is N(3, 2), the total time is N(5+3, 1+2), which is N(8, 3).

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Broadening'
sections.content: Display an animation where two narrow bell curves combine to form a wider, taller bell curve. Explain that because variances are additive, uncertainty always increases when you add independent sources of randomness.
sections.example: Visual overlay of the two initial narrow peaks transforming into one flattened, wider peak representing the final total duration.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap the core takeaway: Summing independent Gaussians is mathematically 'closed'—the result never escapes the Gaussian family. Mention applications in error propagation in engineering or finance.
sections.example: In sensor fusion, combining GPS noise (Gaussian) with IMU noise (Gaussian) results in a total system error that is still a predictable, measurable Gaussian Bell Curve.
